Comparison

Best lecture recorder apps for iPhone and Android (2026)

You may not need a new app to record a lecture: Apple’s own guide uses classroom lectures as an example for Voice Memos, which transcribes the recording on iPhone 12 or later, and Google’s Recorder does the same on Pixel phones. A dedicated lecture recorder helps when you want notes from the class rather than just a transcript, a lecture that runs past an hour handled in one piece, a recording you already have imported, or the same app on iPhone and Android. This page compares nine options using only what each vendor states on its own pages, checked on October 26, 2026.

Free to download, with 60 minutes of transcription every month.

Can I record a lecture on iPhone without another app?

Yes. Apple’s guide to making a recording in Voice Memos mentions classroom lectures as an example and lets you record with the built-in microphone, a headset or an external microphone. On iPhone 12 or later, Voice Memos transcribes the recording in English (all variants), Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, French, German, Japanese, Korean and Chinese; Apple adds that the feature isn’t available in every country or region. You can copy the transcript and search across titles and transcripts, and with Apple Intelligence, Writing Tools can summarize it on supported iPhones.

The Notes app does the same inside a note: tap Record Audio, and Apple’s Notes guide says the speech is transcribed when the device language is one of those languages. If you mainly want to read or search what was said, these may be all you need. They don’t write lecture notes in a set structure, and they don’t run on Android.

What should a lecture recorder app do?

  • Record the whole class in one piece, even with the phone locked or in your bag.
  • Turn the recording into text you can search: the exam date, a definition, the formula on the board.
  • Make study notes from the transcript, without adding material the lecturer didn’t cover.
  • Take a recording you already have, from another app, a file or a video.
  • Handle the language of the class, especially if it isn’t English.

Google Recorder (Pixel)

Google’s Recorder works on Pixel 3 or later and the Pixel Tablet. According to Google’s language page, live transcription on Pixel 6 or later covers English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Hindi and Chinese (Mandarin), and summaries on Pixel 8 or later cover English, Chinese (Mandarin), Hindi, Italian, French, German and Japanese.

A good fit if you have a recent Pixel and record classes in one of those languages.

Otter

Otter (Otter.ai, Inc.) has apps for iPhone and Android, a web app and a desktop app for Mac and Windows. It records and transcribes live, imports audio and video files and writes automatic summaries. Its help center lists English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese and Chinese (Simplified) as supported languages and marks German and Chinese as beta.

A good fit if your classes are in English or another language on its list and you want the same notes on your phone and computer.

Notta

Notta runs on iPhone and Android, on the web and as a desktop app for Windows and macOS (supported environments). The app’s home screen offers Import Files, Record Now and Live Transcribe Meetings, its language list is long, and its App Store listing describes AI summaries.

A good fit if you switch between phone and laptop and take classes in more than one language.

Transkriptor

Transkriptor is available for iOS and Android, on the web, as a Chrome extension and as a desktop app for Windows and Mac. Its App Store listing describes an integrated audio recorder, file transcription (MP3, WAV, M4A), AI summaries and a chat with the transcript.

A good fit if some of your classes are online and you also want a browser extension or a desktop recorder.

Transcribe – Speech to Text (DENIVIP)

Transcribe – Speech to Text (DENIVIP Group OOO, App Store id1241342461) works on iPhone, iPad and Mac and in a web editor at transcribe.com. Its App Store listing describes a built-in recorder with live transcription, audio and video uploads, speaker separation, and AI summaries and key points. Other apps have similar names, so check the developer before you download.

A good fit if you study on an iPhone and a Mac and want to edit transcripts in a browser.

Aiko

Aiko, from the independent developer Sindre Sorhus, turns recordings of meetings, lectures and voice memos into text with OpenAI’s Whisper model running on the device; the developer says the audio is never uploaded. It runs on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Vision Pro, and its App Store listing requires iOS 26 or later.

A good fit if you want the transcript and don’t need a summary, and prefer the audio to stay on your device.

Verbi Lecture Recorder & Notes

Verbi Lecture Recorder & Notes is the App Store name of Verbi, an AI voice recorder and note taker for iPhone and Android. It records the whole class (on iPhone, with the screen locked), imports audio and video files, recordings shared from other apps and YouTube links, and transcribes 39 languages with automatic language detection.

Its Lesson Notes template turns the transcript into notes that follow the class: definitions, rules, formulas, worked examples, and homework or exam dates only when the lecturer mentioned them. It doesn’t add textbook material that wasn’t taught, and marks a term as unclear rather than guessing. With Pro, you can ask a lecture questions (“What did she say about the exam?”), translate it and export it as TXT or PDF. Verbi needs no account; recordings and transcripts are stored on your phone, and the audio is sent to our speech-to-text providers to transcribe it, as the privacy policy explains.

The free plan includes 60 minutes of transcription and 3 AI summaries a month, enough to try it in one class. For a full term, Pro includes 20 hours a month (or 5 a week on the weekly plan), and MAX twice that. Verbi has no web or desktop version. The steps are in the lecture recorder guide.

How do I choose a lecture recorder app?

It depends on what you want after class. Going by the table:

  • A searchable transcript is enough: Voice Memos and Notes on iPhone 12 or later, or Recorder on a Pixel, are already on your phone.
  • Study notes after every class: Otter, Notta, Transkriptor, Transcribe and Verbi write AI summaries; Verbi’s Lesson Notes template is built for lectures and keeps to what was said. Apple and Google summarize on newer devices.
  • Classes in a language Apple or Otter doesn’t list: check the vendor’s own list. Verbi transcribes 39 languages, among them Arabic, Hindi, Turkish and Indonesian, and detects the language for you.
  • iPhone and Android: Otter, Notta, Transkriptor and Verbi have apps on both.
  • Studying at a laptop: Otter, Notta and Transkriptor have desktop apps, and Transcribe has a Mac app and a web editor.
  • Audio that shouldn’t leave the phone: Aiko transcribes on the device. For any other app, read its privacy page.
  • Always: check that recording is allowed in your course, and ask the lecturer if you’re not sure.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best app to record lectures on iPhone?

It depends on what you need from the recording. For a searchable transcript, Voice Memos (iPhone 12 or later) is already installed. For study notes after each class, an app with AI summaries such as Otter, Notta, Transkriptor, Transcribe or Verbi fits better; Verbi’s Lesson Notes template keeps to what the lecturer said. The table above compares them using each vendor’s own pages.

Can I record a whole lecture with my phone locked?

In Verbi on iPhone, yes: the recording continues with the screen locked. On Android, keep Verbi open on the recording screen with the screen on. For other apps, check their help pages.

Can an app make lecture notes from an audio recording?

Yes. Import the recording into an app that summarizes transcripts. In Verbi, tap Upload File or share the recording to Verbi, and the Lesson Notes template turns the transcript into notes; the free plan includes 3 summaries a month.

Is it legal to record a lecture?

Rules differ by school, course and place. Check your course policy, and ask the lecturer if you’re not sure.

Can I record lectures on Android?

Yes. Verbi, Otter, Notta and Transkriptor have Android apps, and on Pixel phones Google’s Recorder transcribes several languages as you record.

Who made this comparison?

The team behind Verbi. For the other apps, the table uses only what their own pages, help centers and store listings say; anything they don’t state is marked “—”.
